item.title: IP conference champions open innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Open standards, fair licensing and global cooperation have become keywords at the ongoing 15th China Intellectual Property (IP) Annual Conference. Industry leaders from China and abroad pointed out that innovation thrives on sharing, not shutting others out. Chinese IP heavyweight Huawei said it has greatly benefited from sharing its innovations. The tech giant has accumulated over 160,000 granted patents, generating billions of yuan in annual licensing revenue. "Licensing is not just a legal act. It is a catalyst for open innovation," Fan Zhiyong, Huawei's vice president and chief IP officer, said at the conference on Tuesday. According to Fan, Huawei has contributed many core patented technologies to global industries through fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory licensing. The company recently grabbed global headlines by striking a cross-licensing deal with HP, granting the U.S. firm access to specific Huawei-owned Wi-Fi patents. "Without a licensing system that rewards innovation, many companies would be reluctant to contribute their core technologies to industry standards. They would choose to work behind closed doors," Fan added. He urged other companies to view patent licensing as a "strategic investment" rather than litigation risk. That vision was echoed in the remarks from Xiaomi. Liu Zhen, the company's vice president for legal and international political affairs, said that open-source ecosystems, standard setting and patent protection are key to supporting innovation in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). With its global patents exceeding 47,000, Xiaomi called for an IP ecosystem that is "win-win, sustainable, and can protect innovators while making innovation accessible to more people." Technological isolation leads to repetitive R&D and high costs, and ultimately denies low-income regions access to progress, Liu noted. "Expanding the 'cake' of the industry is far more valuable than holding onto a piece of it." Patrik Hammarén, President of Nokia Technology Standards, voiced a similar view in his speech, describing open, collaboratively developed standards as "one of the great success stories of modern industry." He cited cellular connectivity, Wi-Fi and audio-video codecs as examples of technologies that are not the work of any single company or country, but rather the product of thousands of engineers from companies both large and small. Beyond the world of commerce, many organizations have also adopted this same spirit of cooperation. Carsten Fink, the Chief Economist of the World Intellectual Property Organization, noted that the benefits of innovation extend far beyond the country or region where new technologies are developed. He said China offers a compelling example: once a major beneficiary of global knowledge, it has now become a vital source of innovation for the rest of the world. Chinese investment, manufacturing scale and technological advances have made solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles more affordable and widely accessible, with gains stretching well beyond China's borders. Michael Moore, a board member and treasurer of the International Trademark Association (INTA), welcomed the opportunities for professional dialogue and stakeholder input in China's IP legislative process. He highlighted that sustained dialogue, shared experience and cooperation can help build more trusted, predictable, and effective IP environments. More than 8,000 people attended this two-day conference in Beijing. Many guests from government departments, academia and the business community delivered keynote speeches at over 10 sub-forums. ■

item.title: China services trade fair showcases innovation, promotes openness
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) opened Wednesday in Beijing, as China steps up efforts to expand opening-up in services trade at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Running through Sept. 13 at Shougang Park, a former industrial site and venue for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, the fair has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with over 1,800 companies exhibiting on-site. Among them are 473 Fortune Global 500 firms and other industry leaders, including Honeywell, Johnson & Johnson and Siemens. Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features a Global Trade in Services Summit, co-hosted for the first time by the World Intellectual Property Organization. A series of forums and business matchmaking activities will also be held during the fair. During the summit, Zimbabwean Vice President Constantino Chiwenga said the CIFTIS is expected to create many investment opportunities across conferencing, exhibition, infrastructure, and digital services, adding that it will help Zimbabwe identify opportunities for trade in services, build export capacity, and attract credible partners across technology, finance, tourism, education and health care. Alexander Poulev, deputy prime minister and minister of Economy, Investment and Industry of Bulgaria, said at the summit that trade in services is an important pillar of the China-Bulgarian relationship. "We want to see more Bulgarian products reaching the Chinese market and more Bulgarian companies building long-term partnerships with Chinese businesses," he said. More than 100 new products and services will make their debut at the fair, covering fields such as information and communications, fintech, and digital and intelligent healthcare. Another highlight is a new overseas expansion services roadshow area, which offers Chinese companies one-stop professional support to enter foreign markets and expand the global footprint of Chinese services. The core exhibition area also debuts a showcase of more than 140 innovation cases spanning all 12 categories of services trade, including artificial intelligence, large language models, and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed. China has posted rapid growth in services trade, with strong exports of knowledge-intensive services supported by the country's IP and innovation ecosystem, said World Intellectual Property Organization Director General Daren Tang in his video address to the summit. Latest official data showed that in the first seven months of 2026, China's services trade totaled nearly 4.45 trillion yuan (about 656.6 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.3 percent year on year. Advancing high-quality development of services trade is a key task in the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which calls for intensified efforts to optimize negative list management of services trade, ease cross-border restrictions, encourage services exports, and foster knowledge-intensive services trade. ■

item.title: From spinal implant to cancer therapy, foreign patients seek out China's medical advances
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- After multiple attempts to treat paralysis in her lower limbs in her home country, 12-year-old Russian girl Vera, a pseudonym, traveled to Hangzhou in east China's Zhejiang Province with help from the Russian Embassy in China. There, doctors implanted a domestically developed closed-loop spinal cord neural interface, which amplifies the brain's weak motor signals, helping them bypass the damaged section of the spinal cord and reactivate the muscles needed for walking. After three months of personalized rehabilitation, Vera was able to take assisted steps. "I like the feeling of walking," said Vera, who had been confined to her wheelchair for more than a year since she suffered a severe spinal cord injury in a traffic accident in June 2025 and lost motor function in her lower limbs. She also became the first overseas patient with such an injury to regain assisted walking in China after receiving the neural interface implant, according to doctors who developed the procedure at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Vera's experience is part of a broader trend of foreign patients seeking medical care in China for advanced medicines, therapies and procedures. According to figures from China's National Health Commission, major hospitals in China recorded about 1.28 million visits by international patients in 2025, up 73.6 percent from three years earlier, with the number of patients from Europe and the United States doubling. Officials from several hospitals told Xinhua that, although foreign patients still make up a small share of total hospital visits, their numbers keep growing. Hospitals in different parts of the country have reported a steady increase in foreign patients. China's expanding medical capabilities in oncology, cell therapy, and other cutting-edge treatments, along with its rich clinical experience, have become an important draw. According to data released by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), China approved 76 innovative drugs and 76 innovative medical devices for marketing in 2025, both record highs. By the end of 2025, China had 4,751 innovative drugs under development, accounting for 33.7 percent of the global total and making it the world's largest country in terms of innovative drugs under development. In June, the NMPA approved the world's first CAR-T cell therapy for treating solid tumors. The treatment works by genetically modifying a patient's own immune cells to attack gastric cancer. China's Caijing magazine reported that 59-year-old New Zealander Josh became the first foreign patient in China to receive the therapy. After completing a 1.5-month course of tumor treatment, he returned to New Zealand in mid-August. Just months earlier, doctors in New Zealand had told him that his cancer treatment had failed. Unable to eat, Josh relied on enteral nutrition to stay alive. After receiving the therapy, he is now trying different soups and ice creams as he works on returning to a normal diet. "China is currently one of the world's leaders in cell and gene therapy," said Renat Badaev, a hematologist at Moscow City Clinical Hospital 52. "The level of medical care is very high, and it is clear that enormous efforts have been invested in the development of cutting-edge technologies." During his visit to a Chinese hospital in late July, Badaev said he was impressed by the results of CAR-T therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Another hematologist on the tour, Anastasia Zhernyakova, noted that China has accumulated extensive medical experience, driven by the large number of transplants performed in the country, the substantial volume of CAR-T products manufactured and the large number of patients receiving such therapy. Chen Gao, director of neurosurgery at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, said Vera's case demonstrated how advances in Chinese medical technology can benefit patients beyond the country's borders. He noted that China's progress in neurosurgery and brain-computer interface technology is moving from laboratory research toward more standardized clinical applications, adding that international medical cooperation can help more patients benefit directly from advances in diagnosis and treatment. "Chinese medical solutions should benefit not only people in China, but patients around the world. Medical progress should transcend national borders," Chen said. ■

item.title: China recognizes 11 new occupations as new industries create fresh roles
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China on Wednesday officially recognized 11 new occupations and 23 new specialties under existing occupations, reflecting evolving labor demand driven by technological advances, industrial upgrading and shifting consumer needs. The new occupations, released by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and other government departments, include shore-based ship management engineering technicians, embodied intelligence robot technicians and sports data analysts. Authorities also revised information concerning six existing occupations or specialties, including agricultural product brokers. The recognition of the new occupations and specialties will help promote employment and entrepreneurship, offer workers more diverse career paths and better match talent supply with job demand. Five of the newly recognized occupations are classified as digital occupations and three as green occupations, bringing the respective totals in China to 113 and 142. A ministry official said China is expected to face a sizable shortage of workers with digital skills for some time, adding that the recognition of the new occupations would spur training and open up broad employment prospects. The latest additions also highlight the continued expansion of modern services. Some of these new occupations focus on business development and industrial upgrading, including corporate sustainability planners, airport obstacle-clearance inspectors, and artificial intelligence (AI) agent developers. Others respond more directly to people's demand for higher-quality services, including incense-making artisans, smart furniture assembly and commissioning workers, and fresh-cut flower processing workers. More modern service occupations are expected to emerge amid the increasing specialization and upgrading of producer services and improvements in the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, the official said. New specialties under existing occupations include community workers, low-altitude logistics operators and age-friendly renovation designers. Since 2019, China has released eight batches of 121 new occupations. Of these new occupations, 60 percent were service-related, while professional and technical occupations and manufacturing-related occupations each accounted for 17 percent. By industry, 43 percent of the new occupations were in modern services, while 34 percent were in advanced manufacturing. The ministry said it will formulate national standards for the new occupations to guide vocational education, skills training and talent assessment. During the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China aims to explore new employment space in the digital economy, green economy and silver economy. ■

item.title: Factbox: Latest relief and rescue progress at mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, causing heavy casualties and leaving many missing. Chinese rescuers immediately launched all-out search and rescue operations. Here is what we know about the deadly mudslide and the latest progress in China: -- As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, a total of 43 people had been confirmed dead and 519 others remained missing in the disaster. A total of 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries have been identified among the missing. -- The fourth batch of emergency relief supplies from China to Nepal was dispatched on Tuesday morning, including equipment for transportation and lighting and mortuary supplies, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Tuesday. The China Foundation for Rural Development has sent people to the affected communities in Nepal to set up temporary shelters and provide daily necessities and basic medical services. The Chinese Enterprises Association in Nepal recently delivered the first batch of funds donated for relief operations, she added. -- A total of 444 residents evacuated from nearby villages in Gyirong Town have safely returned home after the threat from a barrier lake was largely eliminated. Over the past several days, experts have conducted safety inspections and hydrological monitoring. The barrier lake above the main area of Gyirong Port has been drained, the river has resumed normal flow, and the risk has been largely removed. -- As of 5 p.m. Tuesday, banks had granted credit totaling 79 million yuan (about 11.66 million U.S. dollars) to businesses affected by the disaster and those supporting disaster relief and the provision of essential supplies. They had also issued 32 loans totaling 53.53 million yuan to related businesses and individuals. For borrowers affected by the disaster, the Agricultural Bank of China's Gyirong Port branch granted extensions on 638 loans totaling 114 million yuan. -- Insurers had estimated losses at 450 million yuan, including nearly 200 million yuan under accident insurance and 210 million yuan under non-auto policies such as engineering, liability and property insurance. They had received 142 related claims and paid out more than 4.47 million yuan. ■

item.title: China remains trustworthy partner for other Global South countries: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China is not "pulling up the ladder" behind anyone, a spokesperson said on Wednesday, reaffirming that China will remain a trustworthy partner for the other Global South countries. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing, responding to claims that China only cares about its own development while "pulling up the ladder" behind the other Global South countries. China is dedicated to building ladders for others, Mao said, citing the Belt and Road Initiative, the supply of high-value, low-cost industrial equipment and tech products, and zero-tariff policies. Mao said pursuing mutual benefit and shared success is the defining value of China's international cooperation. The so-called "ladder-pulling" rhetoric finds no traction among Global South countries, the spokesperson said, adding that China will always uphold the principle of mutual benefit and common development and help boost revitalization of the Global South through its own development. ■

item.title: China's inflation edges up, signaling sustained recovery in domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Customers buy goods at a supermarket in Liangyuan District of Shangqiu, central China's Henan Province, Sept. 9, 2026. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, reversing three consecutive months of decline, while the year-on-year gain accelerated from 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, edged up to 1 percent year on year from 0.9 percent the previous month. (Photo by Li Heng/Xinhua) BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's price levels continued their moderate recovery in August, reflecting sustained improvement in domestic demand under supportive policy measures. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, reversing three consecutive months of decline, while the year-on-year gain accelerated from 0.5 percent to 0.8 percent. NBS statistician Dong Lijuan attributed the uptick to several factors: rising energy prices, seasonal increases in food prices, continued gains in travel services during the summer holiday period, and higher prices for smartphones and computers driven by the surging demand for computing power. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy prices, edged up to 1 percent year on year from 0.9 percent the previous month. Factory-gate prices also sent encouraging signals. The producer price index (PPI) rose 0.4 percent month on month in August, swinging from a 0.7 percent decline the previous month, while the year-on-year gain widened to 3.8 percent. The NBS cited the pass-through effect of rising global commodity prices and stronger demand in some sectors driven by domestic industrial upgrading. Wednesday's price data is consistent with the broad pickup in consumer activity seen across China this summer. Railway passenger trips totaled 954 million in July and August combined, and summer box office receipts reached 12.5 billion yuan (1.84 billion U.S. dollars). To channel consumer enthusiasm, more than 30,000 events centered on summer leisure, study tours and night economy were held nationwide, while over 450 million yuan in consumption subsidies were distributed by local governments. Expanding domestic demand remains high on China's economic agenda. At a high-level meeting in late July, policymakers called for effectively expanding domestic demand, broadening quality supply to meet the needs of different consumer groups, and tapping the potential of service consumption. The Ministry of Commerce recently issued a set of guidelines to accelerate the release of demand for personalized consumption. Experts believe more efforts should be made to smooth the flow of consumption and lift income expectations of individuals. Chasing Securities predicts the policy measures to continue driving a moderate recovery in price levels. Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating, forecasts that CPI will continue to edge up year on year in September, with price levels expected to remain moderate. The role of consumption as a primary engine of economic growth is set to strengthen. Official data showed final consumption expenditure contributed 2.1 percentage points to GDP growth in the first half of the year, continuing to lead all growth drivers. For the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China has released a dedicated consumption expansion plan setting out 28 priority measures, with efforts to cultivate new consumption models and scenarios, raise household spending capacity, and optimize the consumer environment. A strong domestic demand helps ensure a stable economy. With expanding domestic demand as a strategic anchor, China's pro-consumption policies will inject sustained internal growth momentum into the broader economy, experts said. ■ Customers select vegetables at a market in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Sept. 9, 2026. item.title: Xi extends congratulations over DPRK's 78th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chinese president, on Wednesday extended congratulations to Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK) and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), over the DPRK's 78th founding anniversary. In his message, Xi pointed out that over the past 78 years, under the leadership of the WPK, the DPRK people have achieved vigorous development in various fields of socialist construction through self-reliance, unity and hard work. In recent years in particular, under the leadership of Kim, the WPK and the DPRK people have made every effort to advance economic and social development, scoring a series of development achievements to China's heartfelt delight, said Xi. Xi expressed confidence that the brotherly DPRK people will surely achieve the goals and tasks set forth at the Ninth Congress of the WPK and continuously open up new prospects for the cause of Party and state development. China and the DPRK are friendly socialist neighbors who stand by each other and share weal and woe, Xi said, stressing that it is an unswerving policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to preserve, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. Xi noted that in June this year, he paid a state visit to the DPRK and met with Kim again, opening a new chapter in the development of relations between the two Parties and the two countries. Xi said that he stands ready to work together with Kim to continue strengthening the strategic guidance of relations between the two Parties and the two countries, jointly promote the development of their respective Party and state causes, continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples and deepen their friendship, so as to make greater contributions to promoting peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region and the world at large. ■

item.title: Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended greetings to teachers and educators across the country ahead of Teachers' Day, which is celebrated annually on Sept. 10. In a congratulatory message, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called on teachers nationwide to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation. Over long periods of time, teachers across the country have devoted themselves to education, imparting knowledge and nurturing young minds, said Xi, commending their significant contributions to the cause of the Party and the state. Xi emphasized the importance of carrying out the basic task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating a high standard of professional integrity and conduct on the new journey. He also called for fostering public respect for educators, encouraging support for education, and bringing together all efforts to make China a leading country in education. China boasts the largest education system in the world, having roughly 440,000 schools at all levels and of all types, with 280 million students and 18.7 million teachers. ■
